scope: Route A: finite-day centralized scheduling and mechanism analysis in the original simulated Game map
primary_question: At equal trip service and initial/terminal battery requirements, when do route and charging flexibility change resource use, cost and peak load?

hypotheses.H1: Joint flexibility weakly improves the solved user objective when the baseline is feasible and feasible sets are nested; strict improvement in each physical metric is not assumed.
hypotheses.H2: Fixed grid energy and fixed carbon intensity imply invariant emissions under charging time shifts.
hypotheses.H3: Retail pricing can redistribute payments without reducing resource cost.
hypotheses.H4: Capacity, parking windows, congestion assumptions and candidate routes determine feasible service and the magnitude/direction of benefits.

terminal_energy_rule: equal to initial stored energy per vehicle at the end of the full finite day
station_access: Each endpoint uses the nearest actual scene charger. Its declared straight-line driveway joins the nearest node in the vehicle road component; all access driving is included. This driveway is a simulation abstraction, not an independently verified legal road. All arms use the same declared parking sites.
trip_schedule: Finite alternating trips using source departure, source travel span, turnaround rule and min/max legs. Reserve the declared travel span as the deadline; stop adding complete trips at the source simulation end.
routing: Full original generator topology; candidates are shortest-time plus shortest-energy routes. Route time is a declared scenario cost, not endogenous dynamic traffic equilibrium.
price_policy: Wholesale and retail curves are declared simulation inputs; retail = wholesale + 0.25 CNY/kWh in fixed-price comparisons.
baseline: Shortest-time feasible candidate route; first-available charging in each parking window. Additional earliest-deadline greedy and centralized fixed-route comparisons expose baseline dependence.
statistics: Deterministic scenarios are not repeated as statistical replicates. Perturbed input cases use paired seeds; confidence intervals refer to those generated inputs only.
claims_retired: real-world/online/independent traffic validation from Unreal replay
external_validity: This protocol defines missing simulation inputs transparently. It does not turn them into field observations or empirical calibration.
